title: Bill 17 advocacy and rooftop solar support
subtitle: Municipal support for six industrial solar sites and an affordable housing cost-sharing agreement with Kitchener Housing Inc.
overview: At a short special meeting, Council asked the Province of Ontario to consult municipalities further on Bill 17 before it is fully implemented. Council also asked that any review consider the financial effects on cities, so that municipalities stay financially whole. The resolution backs recommendations from the Association of Municipalities of Ontario and was passed {{vote:m1}}. Copies go to the Premier, the housing minister, AMO and Ontario Big City Mayors.

Council endorsed two municipal support resolutions for rooftop solar on six industrial properties near Strasburg Road, Trillium Drive, Steckle Place and Shirley Avenue. The projects are part of a provincial electricity procurement, and the Mayor and Clerk may sign the paperwork {{vote:m2}}. Staff described them as low impact, with no added cost to the city. The power feeds the provincial grid.

After a closed session, Council authorized the Chief Administrative Officer to approve and sign a cost-sharing agreement with Kitchener Housing Inc. for affordable housing {{vote:m4}}. Details were not made public in the minutes.

decisions.detail: Council backed AMO's call for the Province to consult municipalities further and protect their finances before fully implementing Bill 17, and directed that the resolution be sent to provincial and municipal bodies.
Council endorsed municipal support resolutions for rooftop solar at six industrial properties under the provincial LT2 procurement and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the related documents.
Council authorized the Chief Administrative Officer to approve and execute a cost-sharing agreement with Kitchener Housing Inc., to the City Solicitor's satisfaction.

debate: On Bill 17, the sponsoring councillor explained that the motion was revised to align with the Association of Municipalities of Ontario's position. The final whereas clause was removed and the therefore clause was narrowed to consultation and financial protection for municipalities. It passed without recorded discussion.

On solar, one councillor asked when the city would decline to endorse such a project. Staff said each application would be reviewed individually, and that a single-building rooftop installation would only need a building permit.

Several councillors said a blanket or streamlined approach to endorsing rooftop solar could give the market certainty. Staff said they would look into a broader approach, but recommended endorsing these two now.

Staff said a community benefit agreement was considered but not recommended. They cited no added infrastructure or service costs, and no environmental or aesthetic concerns. The local utility was consulted and had no concerns.

Councillors asked whether the power stays local. Staff said it goes into the grid, which supports local resilience, but it is part of the province-wide system. Some councillors urged closer collaboration with the local utility and using performance data to promote more projects.
